name: iron-proxy-564f7bac-blind30-ots
instr:
# Iron: thirty undocumented behaviour changes to find without a test suite

An application that reaches outside its own machine sends its traffic through this program, which reads what the caller sent, decides whether it may go out, attaches whatever credential the far side expects, and passes it along. Nothing about the protocols changed and nothing about the callers changed, yet calls that used to be served correctly now come back wrong, and in several places a call that used to be served is refused outright. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything that has been observed going wrong, described by what was done and what came back.

Much of this shows up while bringing the service up and handing it its settings. Started with nothing but the three mandatory environment variables set, it now yields one numeric default at twice its documented value, while the listen addresses, log level, cache size and timeout defaults all come out as before. Naming an intermediary for outbound encrypted traffic together with a list of hostnames that should bypass it no longer works: a call to a hostname on that list still goes through the intermediary, and when the surrounding environment supplies its own bypass list, the list written in the settings file wins instead of the environment's.
